item.text:
This pass closed the last untested fault-tolerance scenario: whether a witness can actually carry an election after the leader is lost.

**New test: witness-based election after leader loss** (`TestAuditWitnessVotesInElection`, audit-tagged root test)

Upstream's `testWitnessIO` uses one regular node plus one witness, where the witness can only acknowledge writes — it can never supply an election vote, so witness voting was only covered at the raft unit level. The new test builds two regular nodes plus one witness, stops the leader's NodeHost, and requires:

- the surviving regular node to be elected (quorum 2 of 3 needs the witness's vote), and
- a new proposal to commit afterwards (again needing the witness's ack).

Observed: leader node 1 stopped → node 2 elected with the witness's vote → proposal committed. Passes 5/5. (The first run only failed because my harness double-stopped a NodeHost, not because of the implementation.)

**State**

- Findings unchanged: F1 (`(*nodeUser).ReadIndex` misses the engine wakeup), F2 (`handleCandidateReadIndex` records a dropped ReadIndex twice), F3 (`pb.Update.HasUpdate` ignores dropped read indexes). All have executed reproductions and a verified minimal fix in `audit/diag-fixes/` with no regressions.
- The negative-result catalogue now also covers witness elections alongside the protocol fuzz, in-memory model, vote-restart, entry encoding, follower and observer reads, leader transfer and 1–32 MB payloads.
